newsitem.title: USA: Blowout Nextlink deal shows U.S. junk mart muscle.
newsitem.headline: Blowout Nextlink deal shows U.S. junk mart muscle.

text.p: A blowout offering of preferred stock exchangeable for junk bonds by Nextlink Communications Inc priced on Tuesday reflects continued proof of the strength of the U.S. high-yield corporate bond market, sources say.
Pegasus Communications Corp, a Radnor, Penn.-based media company, plans to offer $100 million of similar securities on Wednesday via CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp.
Nextlink, which originally planned to offer $125 million, more than doubled the size of its offering on Tuesday as a result of strong investor demand, market sources said.
The preferred stock was priced with a 14 percent dividend rate. The dividends are paid by issuing new securities or pay-in-kind (PIK) for the first five years. Subsequently, they pay in cash.
"These PIK preferreds are coming 250-300 basis points behind cash-pay notes for the same company. Investors have a chance to pick up yield which is hard to find in this market."

The offering also included contingency warrants for five percent of the company. The warrants become exercisable if Nextlink does not raise $75 million through an equity offering by February 1 of 1998.
Nextlink may exchange the preferred stock for junk bonds, paying 14 pecent coupons at any time.

An analyst noted that in the current bullish high-yield market, investors are willing to take the risks of buying preferred stock that offer less protection than bonds in the event of a bankruptcy, "so long as they are positive on the industry and the (company's) story."

Nextlink, based in Bellevue, Wash., is a competitive long distance exchange carrier. It plans to use the proceeds from the offering to build out its network. Merrill Lynch & Co and Toronto Dominion (USA) Securities Inc underwrote the deal.
Price talk on the Pegasus deal is around 12.625 percent, sources say. The deal, expected to price this afternoon, will also include warrants to purchase two percent of the company.
Turning to the U.S. high-grade corporate bond market, syndicate officials said 15-20 banks were considering whether to issue trust preferred deals in the near term.
NationsBank Capital Trust III, a subsidiary of NationsBank Inc, sold $500 million of 30-year, floating-rate trust preferred stock on Wednesday at 55 basis points over Libor.
NationsBanc Capital Markets, Lehman Brothers Inc and Bear Stearns & Co Inc served as joint lead managers.

Bear Stearns is still in the market for a $150 million trust preferred deal, market sources said. The 30-year securities have fixed interest rates for five years and then convert to Libor-floaters, they note.
Great Western Financial also plans to sell $200 million in 30-year trust preferred securities via Goldman Sachs, sources said.
Elsewhere, Union Tankcar is expected to sell $150 million in 10-year bullet bonds via Salomon Brothers Inc on Wednesday, according to market sources.
Union Dominion Realty may sell $100 million in notes due 2007 via a Goldman Sachs-led sydnicate.
Baxter International Inc is expected to sell $250 million in 10-year bonds and $200 million in 30-year bonds via Goldman Sachs & Co later this week or next week.
